title: Unnamed Tracking

panels.title: Scrape health
panels.description: Worst state across the selected instances. Missing measurements remain unknown; they are not treated as healthy.

panels.title: Application ready
panels.description: Worst state across the selected instances. If any selected scrape target has no measurement, the aggregate is unknown instead of silently reporting the other targets as healthy.

panels.title: Database
panels.description: Worst state across the selected instances. If any selected scrape target has no measurement, the aggregate is unknown instead of silently reporting the other targets as healthy.

panels.title: Plugin runtime
panels.description: Worst state across the selected instances. If any selected scrape target has no measurement, the aggregate is unknown instead of silently reporting the other targets as healthy.

panels.title: HTTP traffic Â· route filter applies here
Requests per second by status class
Response start latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Measured until the response starts; response-body transfer is not included. Quantiles need observations in the rate window.

panels.title: 5xx and 429 responses by route
panels.description: Uses the dedicated 429 counter as well as 5xx responses. Empty series can mean no matching errors have been observed; they do not prove that a route was exercised.

panels.title: In-flight requests
panels.description: Current requests across all routes on each selected instance. This unlabelled gauge cannot be narrowed by the HTTP route filter.

panels.title: Unhandled exceptions per second
panels.description: Unhandled exceptions recorded by the host; empty means no series has been created, not an end-to-end error test.

panels.title: Authentication quota decisions
panels.description: Quota decisions include allowed, limited, unavailable, busy and refunded. They are not sign-in success/failure counts.

panels.title: Unexpired browser sessions
panels.description: Active and revoked sessions that have not expired. Snapshot values are cached; replicas can report the same shared database counts and must not be summed.

panels.title: Database pool connections
panels.description: Per-process SQLAlchemy pool state. This collector is absent in multiprocess mode.

panels.title: Dependency health history
panels.description: Cached dependency probes: one is reachable and zero is unavailable.

panels.title: Database probe duration
panels.description: Time spent on the cached database/session/job snapshot, not application query latency.

panels.title: Plugins by state
panels.description: Installed, enabled, healthy and unhealthy are overlapping categories, not parts of a total. Shared runtime counts are not summed across replicas.

panels.title: Plugin runtime errors per second
panels.description: Host-observed errors only. Plugin internals are not exposed by Plugin API v1.

panels.title: Job runs in selected range
panels.description: Prometheus preserves the application job label as exported_job, because job identifies the scrape job. Counters reset on restart and increase() can yield fractional estimates.

panels.title: Time since last successful job
panels.description: Persisted last-success timestamps. A missing series means no recorded successful run; job names use Prometheus exported_job.

panels.title: Job duration (p95)
panels.description: Recorded host maintenance jobs only. Infrequent jobs can have no observations in the rate window.

panels.title: Metadata provider calls by outcome
panels.description: Built-in provider calls only; zero rate can mean no provider requests during the rate window.

panels.title: Metadata provider latency (p95)
panels.description: A provider with no recent calls has an undefined quantile; gaps are retained instead of drawing false zero-latency values.

panels.title: Process CPU (one core = 100%)
panels.description: CPU seconds per wall-clock second. One is one fully used CPU core; values can exceed 100%. Standard process collectors are absent in multiprocess mode.

panels.title: Process resident memory
panels.description: Resident memory in bytes, on its own scale. This collector is absent in multiprocess mode.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: Current worker uptime. Counters can reset when the worker restarts. This collector is absent in multiprocess mode.

panels.title: Response completion and transfer · HTTP route filter applies
Completed responses (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Request entry through the final accepted ASGI body send. Excludes streams, failures and background tasks; this is not browser paint or an SLO.

panels.title: Response start vs completion (p95)
panels.description: Independent distributions: response-start samples include all started kinds/outcomes. Do not subtract percentiles to estimate transfer latency.

panels.title: Terminal responses by kind and outcome
panels.description: Exactly one terminal observation per handled HTTP request. Background errors after completion do not reclassify the response.

panels.title: Streams and event streams (p95)
panels.description: Long stream lifetimes are expected. Do not interpret this panel as interactive page latency.

panels.title: Observed response body throughput
panels.description: Bytes accepted by application ASGI send. Excludes headers/TLS and downstream Nginx compression. Sendfile-extension bytes are unknown and omitted.

panels.title: Consumed request body throughput
panels.description: Only body chunks actually consumed by handlers, with no buffering or extra reads. Not total ingress bytes.

panels.title: Disconnects and cancellations by phase
panels.description: Observed receive disconnects, failed sends and task cancellations. Each response contributes at most once; a cancellation is not proof the browser disconnected.

panels.title: Slowest completed response routes (p95)
panels.description: Ordinary completed responses only, grouped by fixed route template. Browser execution and image decoding are outside this measurement.

panels.title: SQL execution and cache work · deployment/instance scoped
SQL cursor execution (p95)
panels.description: Cursor execution only: excludes pool checkout and result decoding. No SQL text, table, parameter or account labels. HTTP route filter does not apply.

panels.title: SQL executions by outcome
panels.description: One execution observation per database cursor operation, including errors and cancellation. HTTP route filter does not apply.

panels.title: Cache lookup outcomes
panels.description: Fixed cache kinds only. Bypass is excluded from the hit ratio; negative metadata results count as hits. No storage inventory is inferred.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Hit + negative-hit / all non-bypass lookups. Missing or idle series stay unknown; this does not estimate saved upstream bytes.

panels.title: Cache fetch/rebuild duration (p95)
panels.description: Metadata fetch/store, artwork-preview resize/store and collection-collage generation. Warm hits are not refreshes.

panels.title: Observed cache removals
panels.description: Only instrumented real removals: metadata expiry replacement / capacity eviction and artwork-preview invalidation. Not a filesystem sweep or inventory.

panels.title: Connection acquisition p95
panels.description: Actual application pool checkout time, including waiting and connection creation; no SQL or account labels.

panels.title: Pool timeouts and rollbacks
panels.description: Application pool exhaustion and completed session rollbacks per second.

panels.title: Measured cache storage
panels.description: Bytes found in a bounded background scan; no configured cache byte budget exists.

panels.title: Upstream cache downloads
panels.description: Actual bytes read from built-in metadata and image providers per second; no saved-byte estimate.

panels.title: Cache inventory available
panels.description: One means the last bounded background inventory completed; zero means the entry and storage gauges are unavailable.

panels.title: Measured cache entries
panels.description: Metadata search is process-local; derived image entries come from the shared volume.

description: Application health, traffic, authentication, plugins, jobs, providers and process resources. Deployment and instance filters apply throughout; HTTP route only affects HTTP panels.
